I read the differing files in both directories. Here is my plan.

**Files that differ**

1. `/workspace/attr/_d

unders.py` (current) vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/attr/_dunders.py` (wanted)
2. `/workspace/tests/test_dunders.py` (current) vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_dunders.py` (wanted)

**

What is wrong for the user today**

In the current version, when a class is built with `attr.s` (or the helper functions in `_d
unders.py`), the generated start-up code calls each attribute's check function with only the value you passed in. A check function therefore cannot tell *

which* attribute it is checking, nor can it look at the attribute's name, its type, or its default value.

In the wanted version, the
same call now hands the check function two pieces of information: the attribute description object itself and the value. So a single check function can be reused across

many attributes and can report the attribute name inside its error message.

The companion test file shows the same difference. Today, in

`/workspace/tests/test_dunders.py`, the check function takes a single argument and the test asserts the error carries just the value 42. In `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_dunders.py`, the check function accepts any number of arguments

, the attribute object is built once and reused, and the test asserts the error carries both the attribute object and the value 42.

**What the ticket should say**

- What happens now

: a check function is only handed the value, so it cannot know which attribute failed or include the attribute name in its error message.
- What should happen: a check function is handed the attribute description and the value, so it knows

which attribute it is checking and can name it in errors.
- About this project: the project is a small library that writes simple data classes for

you; you list your attributes and it writes the start-up method, the text form, equality, and the checks for you.
- Problem this
solves: today I have to write a separate check function for every attribute, because it has no way to tell which one is being checked, and my

error messages cannot say which field was wrong.
- What changed: the generated start-up method now passes the attribute description along with the value into every check function; existing

single-argument check functions will now receive an extra argument, so they need to accept more than one argument.
- Impact: usability and correctness of
error messages; this touches every attribute that has a check function, and single-argument check functions will stop working as written

.
- User experience: with a check function that takes one argument, the raised error contains only the value; after the change, the same check function receives the attribute description first and

the value second, and the raised error contains both, so the message can name the offending field.
- Hints (paths from the current workspace only): `/workspace/attr/_dunders.py` and `/workspace/tests

/test_dunders.py`.

**Things to avoid in the ticket**

No code, no code fences, no developer words (implement, refactor, patch, deploy, pull
request, backport, and similar), no phrases like "this change" or "for backward compatibility", and no hedging words (probably, maybe
, seems, likely). Do not mention `.git`, and do not name any file that only exists in the wanted version.
